title: Beta support readiness + messaging for Optimization Suggestions (estimates, risk labels, known issues)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Goal
Align Support + CS on how to message the Optimization Suggestions beta in Console (batching/caching only), including disclaimers, known limitations, and repeatable responses for “estimate is wrong” / “risk level is confusing” feedback.

Background
We are launching a private beta of a Suggestions view that surfaces estimated $ savings, latency deltas, and a Low/Medium/High risk label. Early demos and internal dogfood have already produced predictable questions:
- “Estimated savings doesn’t match billing.”
- “Why is this suggestion High risk?”
- “Suggestions page is empty but we have traffic.”
Support/CS needs a consistent story that is conservative and does not imply contractual savings.

Scope (this ticket)
1) Support/CS enablement pack:
- One-page summary of the feature (what it is / what it is not)
- Standard disclaimers + where they appear (Console + docs)
- Known issues / failure modes + expected user symptoms
- Triage decision tree: estimate mismatch, empty state, RBAC access, latency regression
- Escalation paths and owners (Eng + Applied ML + Telemetry)

2) Response templates/macros (Support + CS):
- “Estimate vs billing” explanation and questions to ask
- “Risk level explanation” and how to frame it as performance/reliability risk (not security)
- “Insufficient telemetry” explanation and what signals are required

3) Internal comms + readiness:
- 30-min training session for Support + CS (recording + notes)
- Quick links to dashboards/runbooks
- Clear “when to escalate” guidelines + required data to include

Non-goals
- Changing the estimator, risk scoring thresholds, or UI copy directly (raise follow-ups if needed).
- Customer-specific savings commitments or ROI guarantees.

Primary collaborators
- Support readiness: Dev Patel (owner)
- CS beta partner: Miguel Santos
- PMs: Marissa Cole (Console), Aditya Rao (Optimize)
- Docs: Elliot Price
- Applied ML: Dr. Maya Srinivasan / Sana Farid (risk + confidence)
- Telemetry: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (data pipeline + attribution)

Proposed disclaimers (draft)
- “Savings and latency impact are estimates based on recent telemetry and model prices; they may differ from invoiced usage due to time windows, discounts/commits, rounding, and workload changes.”
- “Risk reflects potential performance/reliability impact if applied; it does not represent a security risk.”
- “Beta limitations: batching/caching suggestions only; not a guarantee; not auto-applied.”

Known issues / common pitfalls (initial list)
- Billing mismatch: different aggregation windows (UI uses trailing 7d), delayed cost attribution, customer discounts/committed-use pricing, prompt caching effects, changes in traffic mix since the window.
- Empty state with traffic: telemetry lag/backfill gaps; route not emitting required metrics; org/project scoping mismatch; feature flag not enabled.
- Confusing risk: customers interpret as security/compliance; risk label often driven by low latency budgets, high tail sensitivity, or low confidence band.

Acceptance criteria
- Support/CS has a single doc with:
  - disclaimers, known issues, and a triage tree
  - 3 response templates/macros ready to use
  - links to dashboards/runbooks and escalation contacts
- Training session completed; recording link posted in #support and #customer-success.
- PM sign-off from Marissa + Aditya that messaging matches beta positioning and avoids overpromises.

Deliverables/links (to be added during execution)
- Support enablement doc link
- Macro text snippets
- Training recording link

Risks
- If estimate mismatch volume is high, we need a fast path to identify estimator/window/config causes vs actual defects; otherwise Support will churn in back-and-forth.
- Risk label misunderstanding can create internal stakeholder alarm at customers; we need crisp wording + examples.
comments: 2026-02-06 (Dev Patel): Drafted the “what it is / what it isn’t” section and collected top 10 questions from Support queue + sales demos. Next: align with PM on exact wording for “estimate vs billing” so we don’t imply guarantees.

2026-02-07 (Miguel Santos): From Arkadia beta check-in: they want a short, non-technical explanation for exec stakeholders. Suggest adding a 2–3 sentence “executive summary” macro + a deeper technical follow-up template.

2026-02-10 (Aditya Rao): Please be explicit that savings are computed from recent telemetry and assumed unit prices; do not claim we reconcile to invoice line items. Also mention committed-use discounts can cause variance.

2026-02-11 (Logan Wright): Telemetry lag is the #1 cause of “empty but high traffic”. Added checklist: verify ingestion health, last_seen timestamps, and whether the route emits cache metrics (required for caching suggestions).

2026-02-13 (Elliot Price): Added disclaimer block to the docs draft and mirrored the same wording for in-console “Learn how estimates work” link. Request: PM to confirm final copy for “risk is not security risk.”

2026-02-14 (Sana Farid): For risk explanations, recommend including the specific driver(s) when possible (tail latency sensitivity / low confidence / low concurrency / cache volatility). Even if Support can’t see internal drivers, macros can ask the user for route SLO and traffic pattern to contextualize.

2026-02-18 (Dev Patel): Ran training with Support + CS. Key confusion: people were mixing org-level invoices with project-level Suggestions. Updated macro to ask for org, project, route, time window, and whether Dedicated pricing applies.

2026-02-21 (Marissa Cole): Signed off on the messaging pack. Only change: replace “billing doesn’t match” with “invoice totals may differ” and always lead with time window + discounts as the most common reasons.

2026-02-24 (Dev Patel): Marking Done. Enablement pack published, macros added to Support workspace, recording posted. Next step is to monitor volume of estimate-mismatch tickets in the first 2 weeks of beta expansion.
